name: Essential Utilities
headline: A regulated water and gas utility with natural franchises that no competitor can cross.
what_short: Regulated water and natural gas utility
what_it_does: Essential Utilities supplies water and wastewater service and, through Peoples, natural gas in Pennsylvania, Kentucky and other states. Regulated water is its deciding part, and regulated natural gas was 39% of the five-year total the analysis examined. State commissions set the rates, and it plans $8.7 billion of capital spending for 2026 to 2030.
why_it_passed: A water franchise is a natural monopoly held under the state commissions, and the filings show it neither open to a funded attacker nor filling in.
Its earning power is the rate base times a return set in public proceedings, so the ten-year economics can be foreseen in a general way.
Its $8.7 billion capital plan for 2026 to 2030 is published, so the rate base growth is knowable.
The analysis found no doubt about management's honesty: reports were clear, there was no restatement, and an adjustment cut the featured figure.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what Essential Utilities may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At $42.45 a share against a value range of $28.63 to $32.98, a buyer would earn only about 3.6% to 4.5% a year on the cash the business produces, less than a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.30%).
watch: Growth needs about a dollar of new capital for every dollar of growth, at a regulated return, so it needs a constant inflow of new money.
It has paid dividends while selling new stock, and the stock's market return failed the analysis's five-year retention test.

Peoples was bought in 2020 well above book value, and that premium earns nothing in rates; its gas business faces declining use per customer, and at least $450 million of PFAS-related capital is planned.
